abstract: Blood samples for hormone analysis were obtained 5 to 20 years post-therapy from 12 men with testicular tumors who were originally treated by unilateral orchiectomy followed by abdominal and/or pelvic irradiation. In nine patients (75%) the levels of FSH and LH, and in one patient (8%) the testosterone values, were outside the ranges found in age- and sex-matched controls. From this retrospective study we conclude that, even when the remaining testis is kept outside the field of radiation, significant radiation damage occurs, mainly through scatter. This damage is more likely to occur if the hemiscrotum is irradiated. Methods of shielding are available to reduce the dose received by the contralateral testis.
abstract_ja: 治療後5～20年の時点で、片側精巣摘除術と腹部または骨盤への放射線照射を受けた精巣腫瘍の男性12例から、ホルモン分析用の血液検体を採取した。9例（75%）でFSHとLHの値が、1例（8%）でテストステロン値が、年齢と性別をマッチさせた対照群の範囲外であった。後方視的研究であるこの結果から、残存する精巣を照射野外に置いても、主に散乱線によって有意な放射線障害が生じると結論する。この障害は半陰嚢を照射した場合に生じやすい。対側精巣への線量を減らすための遮蔽方法が利用可能である。
